title: Finite pushforward and extension by zero
statement:
Let $\square=(\bar v,v,j_V,j_U,\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 U&\xrightarrow{j_U}&X\\
 v\downarrow&&\downarrow\bar v\\
 V&\xrightarrow{j_V}&Y,
 \end{array}
$$
in which $j_U$ and $j_V$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and $\bar v$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let
$$
 \beta_{\bar v,j_V}:(j_V)_!\,v_*\longrightarrow\bar v_*\,(j_U)_!
$$
be the finite-open comparison map of $\square$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison], a natural transformation of functors $\Ab(U_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ between abelian sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], built from the direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the extensions by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Then for every $G\in\Ab(U_{\Et})$ the morphism
$$
 \beta_{\bar v,j_V,G}:(j_V)_!\,v_*G\longrightarrow\bar v_*\,(j_U)_!G
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$. Consequently $\beta_{\bar v,j_V}$ is a natural isomorphism $(j_V)_!v_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar v_*(j_U)_!$ (its naturality in $G$ is part of [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison]; the inverses $\beta_{\bar v,j_V,G}^{-1}$ are then natural in $G$ as well).

proof.text:
The restricted map $a_G$ is an isomorphism. Put $H:=\bar v_*(j_U)_!G\in\Ab(Y_{\Et})$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison], $\beta_{\bar v,j_V,G}=\varepsilon^!_{j_V,H}\circ(j_V)_!(a_G)$ with
$$a_G=(\Ex^0_{\square,(j_U)_!G})^{-1}\circ v_*(\eta^!_{j_U,G}):\;v_*G\to v_*j_U^{-1}(j_U)_!G\to j_V^{-1}H .$$
The unit $\eta^!_{j_U,G}:G\to j_U^{-1}(j_U)_!G$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso] (Stacks 0F70), so $v_*(\eta^!_{j_U,G})$ is an isomorphism, $v_*$ being a functor [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The exchange morphism $\Ex^0_{\square,(j_U)_!G}:j_V^{-1}\bar v_*(j_U)_!G\to v_*j_U^{-1}(j_U)_!G$ is an isomorphism because $\bar v$ is finite [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] (Stacks 0959), so its inverse exists and is an isomorphism. Hence $a_G:v_*G\to j_V^{-1}H$ is an isomorphism, a composite of two. (This is the identification $j^{-1}f_*j'_!\mathcal F=g_*(j')^{-1}j'_!\mathcal F=g_*\mathcal F$ of the source.)

source.place: Lemma 0GJ1 (etale-cohomology-lemma-compatible-shriek-push-finite, line 11612), proof, second display: 'j^{-1}f_*j'_!F = g_*(j')^{-1}j'_!F = g_*F by Lemmas 0959 and 0F70'

proof.text:
The stalks of $H=\bar v_*(j_U)_!G$ vanish off $V$. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] whose image point $y$ does not lie in $j_V(V)$. Since $\bar v$ is finite, the finite stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] gives
$$H_{\bar y}=(\bar v_*(j_U)_!G)_{\bar y}\cong\prod_{\bar x\in|X_{\bar y}|}((j_U)_!G)_{\bar x},$$
a finite product over the geometric points $\bar x$ of the geometric fibre $X_{\bar y}=X\times_{Y,\bar y}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre], each regarded as a geometric point of $X$ through the projection $X_{\bar y}\to X$, so that $\bar v\circ\bar x=\bar y$ (stalks of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]). No such $\bar x$ has its image point in $j_U(U)$: if $\bar x=j_U\circ\bar u$ for a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$, then $\bar y=\bar v j_U\bar u=j_Vv\bar u$ by the commutativity of $\square$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], so $y=j_V(v(u))\in j_V(V)$, a contradiction. Hence each factor $((j_U)_!G)_{\bar x}$ is $0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] (part 2), and $H_{\bar y}=0$ (an empty product, when $X_{\bar y}=\emptyset$, is $0$ as well).

source.place: Lemma 0GJ1 (etale-cohomology-lemma-compatible-shriek-push-finite, line 11612), proof, first display: '(f_*j'_!F)_y = \bigoplus_{f(x)=y}(j'_!F)_x = 0' for y not in V, by Proposition 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero) and Lemma 0F70

proof.text: Conclusion by the characterization of extension by zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-open-characterization] to the open immersion $j_V:V\hookrightarrow Y$, the sheaves $F:=v_*G\in\Ab(V_{\Et})$ and $H=\bar v_*(j_U)_!G$, and the isomorphism $a:=a_G:F\to j_V^{-1}H$ of step 1; its hypothesis on the stalks of $H$ off $V$ is step 2. It gives that the adjoint morphism $\varepsilon^!_{j_V,H}\circ(j_V)_!(a_G):(j_V)_!v_*G\to\bar v_*(j_U)_!G$ is an isomorphism. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison] this morphism is $\beta_{\bar v,j_V,G}$. (The source concludes 'by the characterization of $j_!$ in Lemma 0F70'; that characterization identifies $j_!g_*\mathcal F$ with $f_*j'_!\mathcal F$ precisely through the adjoint of the restriction isomorphism, which is $\beta$.)

source.place: Lemma 0GJ1 (etale-cohomology-lemma-compatible-shriek-push-finite, line 11612), proof, last sentences: 'Hence by the characterization of j_! in Lemma 0F70 we see that f_*j'_!F = j_!g_*F'

proof.text: Natural isomorphism. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison] the $\beta_{\bar v,j_V,G}$ are the components of a natural transformation $\beta_{\bar v,j_V}$; by step 3 every component is an isomorphism, so $\beta_{\bar v,j_V}$ is a natural isomorphism, and the inverses form a natural transformation: for $\phi:G\to G'$, $\beta_{G'}^{-1}\circ\bar v_*(j_U)_!\phi=\beta_{G'}^{-1}\circ\bar v_*(j_U)_!\phi\circ\beta_G\circ\beta_G^{-1}=\beta_{G'}^{-1}\circ\beta_{G'}\circ(j_V)_!v_*\phi\circ\beta_G^{-1}=(j_V)_!v_*\phi\circ\beta_G^{-1}$. (This is the functoriality whose verification Stacks 0GJ1 omits; here it is built into the definition of $\beta$.)

blueprint_sketch.statement:
In a Cartesian square with $j,j'$ open immersions and $\bar v$ finite,

$$
j_!v_*G\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar v_*j'_!G
$$

is the map of Definition [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison]. It is
functorial in $G$, compatible with identity and composite finite maps, and
commutes with arbitrary base change.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
The preceding lemma proves that the specified map is an isomorphism and
gives both inverse equations.

For a morphism $\phi:G\to H$, naturality is the commutative square

$$
\begin{CD}
j_!v_*G @>{\beta_G}>> \bar v_*j'_!G\\
@V{j_!v_*\phi}VV @VV{\bar v_*j'_!\phi}V\\
j_!v_*H @>{\beta_H}>> \bar v_*j'_!H.
\end{CD}
$$

At $\bar y\in V$, both routes send
$(s_{\bar x})_{\bar x\mapsto\bar y}$ to
$(\phi_{\bar x}(s_{\bar x}))_{\bar x\mapsto\bar y}$; outside $V$ all four
stalks vanish. Thus the square commutes. The same calculation with the
inverse maps $\gamma_G,\gamma_H$ proves naturality of the inverse.

If $\bar v=\operatorname{id}_Y$ and $v=\operatorname{id}_V$, every fibre sum
has one summand. Both the unit–base-change construction of $\beta$ and the
section formula are the identity of $j_!G$. This proves identity
compatibility.

For composition, let $f_1:X_1\to Y$ and $f_2:X_2\to X_1$ be finite. Put
$U_i=X_i\times_YV$, let $g_1:U_1\to V$, $g_2:U_2\to U_1$, and denote the
open immersions by $j_0:V\to Y$, $j_i:U_i\to X_i$. The compatibility to
prove is the outer equality in

$$
\begin{CD}
(j_0)_!(g_1g_2)_*G
@>{\beta_{f_1,g_{2,*}G}}>>
f_{1,*}(j_1)_!g_{2,*}G
@>{f_{1,*}\beta_{f_2,G}}>>
f_{1,*}f_{2,*}(j_2)_!G\\
@V{\beta_{f_1f_2,G}}V{\sim}V
@. @VV{=}V\\
(f_1f_2)_*(j_2)_!G @= (f_1f_2)_*(j_2)_!G
@= (f_1f_2)_*(j_2)_!G .
\end{CD}
$$

At $\bar y\in V$, the upper route first groups a tuple by
$\bar x_1\mapsto\bar y$ and then by
$\bar x_2\mapsto\bar x_1$:

$$
\bigoplus_{\bar x_1\mapsto\bar y}
\left(\bigoplus_{\bar x_2\mapsto\bar x_1}G_{\bar x_2}\right)
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus_{\bar x_2\mapsto\bar y}G_{\bar x_2}.
$$

It is the canonical flattening of the doubly indexed finite sum. The lower
route is the same flattening for the composite fibre. Outside $V$ every
term is zero. This proves composition compatibility; applying the reverse
grouping proves the corresponding equation for $\gamma$.

Finally let $h:\widetilde Y\to Y$ be arbitrary and put tildes on all four
schemes and maps after base change. If $h_X,h_V,h_U$ are the projections,
open and finite base change give the vertical isomorphisms in

$$
\begin{CD}
h^{-1}(j_Y)_!v_*G
@>{h^{-1}\beta_{\bar v,j_Y,G}}>>
h^{-1}\bar v_*(j_X)_!G\\
@V{\sim}VV @VV{\sim}V\\
(\widetilde j_Y)_!\widetilde v_*h_U^{-1}G
@>{\beta_{\widetilde{\bar v},\widetilde j_Y,h_U^{-1}G}}>>
\widetilde{\bar v}_*(\widetilde j_X)_!h_U^{-1}G .
\end{CD}
$$

The left vertical map is
$h^{-1}(j_Y)_!\cong(\widetilde j_Y)_!h_V^{-1}$ followed by
$h_V^{-1}v_*\cong\widetilde v_*h_U^{-1}$; the right vertical map uses the
same two comparisons in the other order. At a geometric point of
$\widetilde V$, both routes pull each component $s_{\bar x}$ to the
corresponding component over the pulled-back geometric fibre. Off
$\widetilde V$, both routes are zero. The rectangle therefore commutes,
and the inverse rectangle follows from the two inverse equations. This
supplies the functoriality omitted at Tag `0GJ1`.

split_report.summary: Statement made precise: the square, G and beta named as in def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison; the claim is that every component beta_G is an isomorphism, hence beta a natural isomorphism (naturality cited from the definition node). The compatibilities with identity and composite finite maps and the stability under extension of the ground field were dropped: of the three listed users, prop-weil-pbc-algebraically-closed-extension step 7 uses only that beta_E is an isomorphism; prop-weil-pbc-proper-curve-sepclosed-invariance no longer cites this node (only blueprint_uses); lemma-weil-pbc-normalization-exact-sequence (imported, not reached by the target) invokes 'the compatibilities' only in a vague naturality-in-field-extension sentence and is to state what it needs at its own split. Proof rewritten after Stacks Lemma 0GJ1 itself rather than the agent paragraph: (1) a_G is an isomorphism (unit of j_! -| j^{-1} iso, Stacks 0F70, new node lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso; finite exchange 0959); (2) stalks of vbar_*(j_U)_!G vanish off V (finite stalk formula, stalks of j_!, commutativity of the square); (3) beta is the adjoint of a_G, so the characterization of j_! (Stacks 0F70 second part, new node lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-open-characterization) makes it an isomorphism; (4) natural isomorphism. This avoids computing beta on stalks as the identity of a direct sum (the brief's step 4): the source's argument never needs it, and the Lean (isIso_finiteOpenComparison_app) argues the same way. Dropped proof_deps: lemma-weil-pbc-curve-locally-constant-reduction (pointer, unused), lemma-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison-inverse (the blueprint's explicit inverse, not needed), lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative (now used inside the characterization node), def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero (moved to stmt_deps).
